clues: This city sits where three rivers meet, in the east of a wide northern land. Thick woods once ringed it, far from the sea.
Winters bite hard here, when polar air drops the cold far below freezing. Summers flip the tale, with hot wet air and heat waves in July.
In 1857 a queen chose this far off lumber town as the new capital. Its deep woods and lone spot helped it please both halves of the land.
In winter, the canal through this city freezes into the world's largest skating rink. Folks skate on the thick ice for mile after mile, right through town.
The parliament of Canada writes the laws of the land in this city. The prime minister and the top court work here too.
